transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. Before we finalize the broadcast plan for Saturday's charity gala, I need to make sure we follow our standard final sign-off procedure. That means I'll need a verbal check with engineering and clearance to confirm the applicable licensing terms and any production changes. Let's start there -- can engineering and clearance confirm they're ready for the sign-off?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: During this morning's final radio-frequency scan, I found that the wireless podium microphone intermittently overlaps the venue's emergency-communications channel. The podium must use the tested wired microphone instead. I recorded the scan in the engineering worksheet, but it hasn't been circulated to the production team yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a critical clearance issue to flag. I confirmed with Northstar Archives this afternoon that the gala's licensed archival clip may be streamed live only to viewers in the United States, may not remain available as a replay, and requires the on-screen credit exactly 'Courtesy of Northstar Archives.' I have the licensor's email in the clearance inbox but haven't copied it into the broadcast plan yet. This directly conflicts with the draft distribution plan, which calls for worldwide streaming and a seven-day replay. Both the territory scope and the replay availability need to be revised before we can approve this plan.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Jules to circulate the RF scan worksheet documenting the wireless microphone conflict to the production team.
Rina to copy the Northstar Archives licensor email and updated clearance terms into the broadcast plan.
Update distribution plan to reflect U.S.-only streaming, no replay, wired podium microphone, and on-screen credit 'Courtesy of Northstar Archives.'
